  • Single-shell resonance explorer
  • View page source

You can interact with this notebook online: Launch notebook

Single-shell resonance explorer

This notebook follows one packet on a straight path through one shell. Each lesson chooses the radial velocity law, the line target and the launch position, then plots where the projected velocity of the packet meets the target. All lengths and velocities use illustrative units.

Symbol

Variable

Meaning

\(r_\text{in}\), \(r_\text{out}\)

inner_radius, outer_radius

Shell edges

\(m\), \(q\)

velocity_slope, velocity_intercept

Radial law \(v(r) = m r + q\)

\(b\)

impact_parameter

Closest distance of the ray to the centre

\(x_0\)

launch_position

Signed launch coordinate along the ray

\(w\)

line_target_velocity

Projected velocity of the line, \(w = c\,(1 - \nu_\text{line} / \nu_\text{packet})\)

\(s_\text{stop}\)

scatter_distance

Flight distance to an assumed electron scatter

The position along the ray is \(x = x_0 + s\), where \(s\) is the flight distance. The radius is \(r = \sqrt{x^2 + b^2}\). The packet sees the projected velocity

\[v_\parallel(x) = m x + \frac{q x}{\sqrt{x^2 + b^2}},\]

and its projected gradient is

\[G = m + \frac{q b^2}{r^3}.\]

A resonance is a point where \(v_\parallel(x) = w\). The plot shows where resonances can occur. It does not compute whether the packet interacts with the line.

Reading the plot

calculate_distance_line_nonhomologous in tardis/transport/geometry/calculate_distances.py squares the resonance equation into a quartic and returns its four roots. The legend in each plot names the markers for these roots.

[1]:

%matplotlib inline

from math import sqrt

from tardis.visualization.widgets.resonance_explorer.analysis import analyze_case
from tardis.visualization.widgets.resonance_explorer.model import ExplorerInputs
from tardis.visualization.widgets.resonance_explorer.render import render_guided_case

# Common shell and oblique packet ray shared by every lesson
inner_radius, outer_radius = 1.0, 3.0
impact_parameter = 1.2
outer_edge_launch = -sqrt(outer_radius**2 - impact_parameter**2)

Initializing tabulator and plotly panel extensions for widgets to work

1. Homologous expansion

Inputs: \(m = 1\) and \(q = 0\). The radial velocities at the shell edges are 1 and 3.

In the plot: The projected velocity is \(v_\parallel = x\) and the gradient is \(G = 1\) everywhere. The packet meets the target once, at \(x = 0.3\). When \(q = 0\), solve_resonance_quartic returns this root twice, so two markers sit at the same point. Its other two return values are NaN and have no marker.

[2]:

velocity_slope = 1.0
velocity_intercept = 0.0
line_target_velocity = 0.3
launch_position = outer_edge_launch

flight = ExplorerInputs(
    r_in=inner_radius,
    r_out=outer_radius,
    v_in=velocity_slope * inner_radius + velocity_intercept,
    v_out=velocity_slope * outer_radius + velocity_intercept,
    b=impact_parameter,
    x_0=launch_position,
    w=line_target_velocity,
)
homology_analysis = analyze_case(flight)

print(f"Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)={flight.v_in:g}, v(r_out)={flight.v_out:g}")
render_guided_case(homology_analysis)

Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)=1, v(r_out)=3

[2]:

2. Linked nonhomology

This lesson changes only \(q\) from lesson 1. The plot draws lesson 1 as a comparison curve.

Change from lesson 1: \(q = -2.34375\). The radial velocities at the shell edges become \(-1.34375\) and \(0.65625\).

In the plot: \(G = 0\) at \(x = -0.9\) and \(x = 0.9\), so the projected velocity changes direction twice. The packet meets the target three times, at \(x = -1.5559\), \(-0.3415\) and \(2.3955\).

The fourth real root, at \(x = 0.1018\) (grey ▲), solves the squared equation

\[(m x - w)^2 (x^2 + b^2) - q^2 x^2 = 0\]

but not the original equation

\[m x + \frac{q x}{\sqrt{x^2 + b^2}} = w,\]

because squaring removes the sign of \(q x / \sqrt{x^2 + b^2}\).

[3]:

velocity_slope = 1.0
velocity_intercept = -2.34375
line_target_velocity = 0.3
launch_position = outer_edge_launch

flight = ExplorerInputs(
    r_in=inner_radius,
    r_out=outer_radius,
    v_in=velocity_slope * inner_radius + velocity_intercept,
    v_out=velocity_slope * outer_radius + velocity_intercept,
    b=impact_parameter,
    x_0=launch_position,
    w=line_target_velocity,
)
analysis = analyze_case(flight)

print(f"Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)={flight.v_in:g}, v(r_out)={flight.v_out:g}")
render_guided_case(analysis, homology_analysis)

Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)=-1.34375, v(r_out)=0.65625

[3]:

3. Moving the launch position

Change from lesson 2: \(x_0 = -0.5\).

In the plot: The root at \(x = -1.5559\) is now behind the launch position, so the packet never reaches it (amber ✕). Two resonances remain, at \(x = -0.3415\) and \(2.3955\), with one change of direction at \(x = 0.9\) between them. The quartic still returns the same four roots as in lesson 2.

[4]:

velocity_intercept = -2.34375

[4]:

Change from lesson 2: \(x_0 = 1.2\).

In the plot: The roots at \(x = -1.5559\) and \(-0.3415\) are behind the launch position (amber ✕). The path from \(x_0\) has no change of direction and one resonance, at \(x = 2.3955\).

[5]:

4. Moving the line target

Change from lesson 2: \(w = 0.7\).

In the plot: The target is above the highest projected velocity on the path, so the packet meets no resonance. The root at \(x = 2.8614\) is outside the shell (amber ✕). The root at \(x = 0.2401\) has the wrong sign (grey ▲). The other two roots are complex.

In the plot: The target touches the peak of the projected velocity at \(x = -0.9\), where \(G = 0\). The quartic has two roots at \(x \approx -0.9\), so two markers sit there. The packet meets the target again at \(x = 2.6399\). The root at \(x = 0.1726\) has the wrong sign (grey ▲).

5. Whole-shell collapse

Inputs: \(m = 1\), \(q = -3.5\) and \(w = 0.6\). The radial velocities at the shell edges are \(-2.5\) and \(-0.5\), so the whole shell moves inward.

In the plot: \(G = 0\) at \(x = -1.225\) and \(x = 1.225\). The packet meets the target twice, at \(x = -2.5717\) and \(-0.3312\). The root at \(x = 3.9488\) is outside the shell (amber ✕). The root at \(x = 0.1541\) has the wrong sign (grey ▲).

The radial velocity is negative everywhere, but the projected velocity along the ray still changes direction twice.

[8]:

velocity_slope = 1.0
velocity_intercept = -3.5
line_target_velocity = 0.6
launch_position = outer_edge_launch

flight = ExplorerInputs(
    r_in=inner_radius,
    r_out=outer_radius,
    v_in=velocity_slope * inner_radius + velocity_intercept,
    v_out=velocity_slope * outer_radius + velocity_intercept,
    b=impact_parameter,
    x_0=launch_position,
    w=line_target_velocity,
)
analysis = analyze_case(flight)

print(f"Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)={flight.v_in:g}, v(r_out)={flight.v_out:g}")
render_guided_case(analysis)

Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)=-2.5, v(r_out)=-0.5

[8]:

6. Homologous collapse

Inputs: \(m = -1\), \(q = 0\) and \(w = 0.6\). The radial velocities at the shell edges are \(-1\) and \(-3\).

In the plot: \(v_\parallel = -x\) and \(G = -1\) everywhere. The packet meets the target once, at \(x = -0.6\). As in lesson 1, the quartic returns this root twice.

This lesson is the collapsing version of lesson 1. It does not change one input from lesson 5.

)

print(f"Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)={flight.v_in:g}, v(r_out)={flight.v_out:g}")

[9]:

7. Special cases in the solver

Each case below makes the solver take a separate branch, or ends the flight with an electron scatter.

Change from lesson 2: \(b = 0\) and \(x_0 = -3\). The packet moves inward along a radius.

In the plot: solve_resonance_quartic takes its \(b = 0\) branch. The packet meets the target once, at \(x = -2.0438\). The flight ends at the inner shell edge, \(x = -1\), so the packet does not reach the root at \(x = 2.6437\) (amber ✕). The two roots at \(x = 0\), the centre, are outside the shell (grey ▲).

[10]:

velocity_slope = 1.0
velocity_intercept = -2.34375
line_target_velocity = 0.3
launch_position = -3

flight = ExplorerInputs(
    r_in=inner_radius,
    r_out=outer_radius,
    v_in=velocity_slope * inner_radius + velocity_intercept,
    v_out=velocity_slope * outer_radius + velocity_intercept,
    b=0,  # radial ray
    x_0=launch_position,
    w=line_target_velocity,
)
analysis = analyze_case(flight)

print(f"Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)={flight.v_in:g}, v(r_out)={flight.v_out:g}")
render_guided_case(analysis)

Shell edge velocities: v(r_in)=-1.34375, v(r_out)=0.65625

[10]:

Inputs: \(m = 0\) and \(q = 0.8\), so the radial velocity is 0.8 at both shell edges.

In the plot: calculate_distance_line_nonhomologous solves this case directly and does not call solve_resonance_quartic. It returns one root, at \(x = 0.4854\), where the packet meets the target.

[12]:

Change from lesson 2: \(w = 0.275\) and \(x_0 = -1.6\). The packet scatters off an electron after a flight distance \(s_\text{stop} = 3.2\), at \(x = 1.6\).

In the plot: The packet meets the target at \(x = -0.3084\). The root at \(x = 2.3651\) is past the scatter, so the packet never reaches it (amber ✕). The root at \(x = -1.6\) is at the launch position (amber ✕). The root at \(x = 0.0933\) has the wrong sign (grey ▲). The quartic returns all four roots, and the scatter decides which of them the packet meets.

[13]:

Inputs: \(m = 1\), \(q = 0.5\) and \(w = 0.3\).

In the plot: The projected velocity has no change of direction, and the packet meets the target once, at \(x = 0.2127\). The root at \(x = 0.4885\) has the wrong sign (grey ▲). The other two roots are complex.

In this case the discriminant in _solve_resolvent_cubic (tardis/transport/montecarlo/nonhomologous_grid.py) is positive. The sign of that discriminant does not give the number of resonances.

8. Explore on your own

Pick a lesson to load its inputs, then move the sliders. Type in the box beside a slider for an exact value or one outside the slider range. Inputs that analyze_case rejects, such as a launch point outside the shell, leave the last plot in place and show the reason under the sliders.
